title: ‘Show How 3M Is 0% at Fault:’ Expert Witness Used ChatGPT to Write Report Defending Company in Deadly Explosion Lawsuit

reading.body:
The failure here is not a model hallucinating facts but a human using a general-purpose language model as a drafting tool while supplying the conclusion in advance. The expert witness prompted the system to produce a report showing a specific party was zero percent at fault, which means the output was shaped by the desired result rather than by independent analysis of the evidence. This is a misuse of a tool outside the conditions it was built for: ChatGPT is not a forensic engineering system, and it has no access to site inspection data, material testing, or case-specific technical findings.

The failure entered the legal process at the point where expert testimony is supposed to represent independent professional judgment. That layer of professional independence is the check the legal system relies on. Because the prompts were obtained through discovery, the court process itself, rather than any technical audit, was what exposed the method used to produce the report.

What is not established is whether the report's conclusions are factually wrong, whether 3M directed or knew about the use of ChatGPT, or whether any court has ruled on the admissibility or credibility of the report as a result of this disclosure.

reports.title: ‘Show How 3M Is 0% at Fault:’ Expert Witness Used ChatGPT to Write Report Defending Company in Deadly Explosion Lawsuit

summary:
An expert witness hired by 3M to defend the company in a lawsuit over a deadly Houston explosion used ChatGPT to write major portions of his expert report. The witness's AI prompts, which became public through court documents, revealed he asked the chatbot to create a report showing that 3M was zero percent at fault for the 2020 Watson Grinding facility explosion. The incident killed three people, destroyed approximately 200 homes, and led to a $61 million lawsuit.

The case illustrates how artificial intelligence has entered courtroom proceedings through expert witness testimony and other legal applications. The 2020 explosion was caused by a degraded rubber welding hose that leaked flammable gas. Homeowners sued 3M and Watson Grinding, claiming 3M failed to properly maintain the facility's gas detection system and made other errors contributing to the disaster. The discovery of the witness's embarrassing AI prompts demonstrates that such materials can be obtained during litigation and may damage a defendant's credibility.
